text:
Loose your hair to the playful zephyr,

so that it may repay, oh Cynthia, for a while,

some of the many hours the arrangement usurps,

which adds to it not grace, but weight.


How much more light, than crowned or imprisoned,

it reveals to us, waving without reserve!

And tell me whether in the laws of adornment

art ever answered with such great success.


Let ambitious splendors be offered

by waves and the mines of the Orient

to the hair of insecure kings.


Do not curl or gild yours;

and since it grew upon so free a brow,

let it imitate her pride, let it keep no laws.

translation.title: Loose Your Hair to the Playful Zephyr
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the argument for natural loose hair over jeweled artifice.
